The 425 live rows are almost certainly uploaded compliance documents against real apprentice/employee/host-employer entities, not template-generated output — no code path writes a document_metadata row from document_templates/generate-document. Note: a duplicate, differently-timed CREATE TABLE document_metadata also exists in the older 20260226000002_create_document_storage.sql — two migrations define the same table name; which one is actually live was not verified against the production catalogue in this pass.

Referenced as the canonical WIF implementation in crm7/CLAUDE.md.

what_exists.detail: A fixed-layout @react-pdf/renderer React component that renders a charge-rate schedule PDF straight from calculation data, fully hardcoded (no template_id, no merge_variables, D2C-branded). areas.non_technical_user_can: Nothing, for authoring. A non-technical user (a GTO admin) cannot create a new document template, edit an existing template's merge fields, or configure which Google Doc backs a template through the crm7 UI — the only 'Register Template' button in the app links to a route that does not exist (404). The actual template CONTENT is always authored outside crm7 entirely, in Google Docs, using {{VARIABLE}} placeholder tokens that must be typed exactly right (case-sensitive exact-text match at merge time) — this is arguably harder than markdown, since a mistyped placeholder fails silently (the merge just skips it) rather than erroring. Registering that Google Doc as a usable template (setting google_doc_id, writing the merge_variables JSON schema that names which entity field feeds which placeholder) can only be done by someone running SQL directly against Supabase — there is no admin form for it anywhere in the codebase. What a non-technical user CAN do today: (1) upload an existing file (PDF/photo of a licence, certificate, etc.) as a compliance document via DocumentHub on an apprentice/employee/host-employer page — that is real, working, encrypted, and verifiable; (2) if IT/an engineer has already registered a template with a Google Doc ID, pick that template from a dropdown on the Charge Rate detail page and click 'Generate PDF' to merge live entity data into it — but they cannot create, edit, or fix that template themselves; (3) fill in a Mail Merge 'batch' form that creates a database row and then silently does nothing, since no processor reads it — this will look like it worked and never produce a document.
gaps: No UI to create a document_templates row at all — the sole entry point (/documents/templates/new) is a dead link (crm7/src/pages/documents/templates/index.tsx:48).
No UI to edit an existing template's google_doc_id, merge_variables, or signing_config — these are JSON columns only reachable via direct SQL/migration (supabase/seed/document_templates_seed.sql).

Template content authoring is 100% external (Google Docs) and requires learning a code-like {{PLACEHOLDER}} convention with exact-match, case-sensitive semantics — no in-app rich-text/merge-field editor exists.

A self-service cloning RPC (clone_system_template) and DOCX-upload columns were built at the database layer but have zero UI callers — dead, unwired scaffolding that looks like unfinished work rather than an intentional API-only surface.

Two independent TypeScript type contracts (DocumentTemplate/DocumentRecord in types/documents.ts vs LegacyDocumentTemplate/LegacyDocumentRecord in types/entities.ts) target the SAME physical document_templates/document_records tables via different code paths (generate-document pipeline vs generic CRUD stores) — a drift/consistency risk if either shape changes.
documents/management.tsx has two dead 'Upload Document' buttons (header button with no onClick; EmptyState action with neither onClick nor href) — clickable UI that does nothing.

Mail Merge (communications/mail-merge.tsx) creates mail_merge_batches rows with status='pending' but no backend process anywhere in the repo ever reads/advances that table — the feature has a working front door and no engine behind it.

Naming collision between two unrelated systems both called 'Document Hub': the route /documents/hub (generated/signed documents, document_records) and the component DocumentHub.tsx (uploaded compliance files, document_metadata) — worth resolving before building a unified authoring system so new work doesn't inherit the ambiguity.

document_metadata may be defined by two different migrations under the same table name (20260226000002_create_document_storage.sql and 20260611110200_document_metadata_workflow.sql) — which one is actually live was not verified against the production catalogue in this pass; flag as 'unknown' rather than guessed.

Document generation (System B) is entity-type-narrow: generate-document only resolves merge data for person/apprentice, host_employer, client, and training_contract entity types (generate-document/index.ts:226-275) — any other entity type silently produces an empty entityData object and likely fails required-field validation.
reusable_assets: generate-document edge function's WIF-based Google Docs merge pipeline (crm7/supabase/functions/generate-document/index.ts) — a fully working, security-reviewed template-merge-to-PDF engine; the missing piece is purely the authoring/registration UI in front of document_templates, not the generation engine itself.

DocumentHub.tsx + documentService.ts + useEntityDocuments.ts — a genuinely working, encrypted, audited file-upload and verification system (document_metadata) that could be the storage/attachment layer for a unified authoring system's OUTPUT documents, independent of how the document content itself gets authored.

@react-pdf/renderer, already a working dependency (ChargeRatePdfDocument.tsx) for fully in-house, code-defined PDF layouts with no external Google Docs dependency — a candidate foundation if a WYSIWYG/no-code template designer is wanted instead of the Google-Docs-external-authoring model.

document_templates schema itself (category/subcategory/merge_variables/signing_config/branding_level/requires_guardian_if_minor, plus the self-service source/tags/compliance_reviewed columns from 20260304000006) is a reasonably well-designed data model — the gap is entirely in the missing CRUD UI layer on top of it, not the schema.
clone_system_template RPC — a working SECURITY DEFINER function for tenant-scoped template cloning that could be wired to a real 'Duplicate & customise' UI action with minimal backend work.

what_exists.detail: A genuinely well-built, email-client-safe D2C shell (tables not flexbox, inline styles not style blocks, hex not oklch, no pure white/black) added 2026-08-07 in response to an explicit operator complaint ('outbound email is a white page and some text'). It auto-wraps any body_html fragment passed through email-dispatcher or send-notification when source=='platform', but is pure server-side code -- no UI surfaces it, no template author can see or control it, and it explicitly does NOT apply to source=='user' sends (a person's own connected mailbox) by design.

what_exists.detail: Both build their own complete html documents in TypeScript template literals, so email-dispatcher's 'already a full document' check (dispatcher/index.ts:243) passes them through unwrapped -- each is an independently-maintained, drifting reimplementation of the same branded-shell idea. invoice-send-direct's version is the worse of the two: it uses a style block, CSS grid/flexbox for the totals layout, and inline oklch() colors in the header background -- all three are things the shared shell's own doc-comment (email-layout.ts:14-24) explicitly says are broken in Outlook/Gmail, and it uses a light theme entirely inconsistent with the dark D2C shell used everywhere else. This is a concrete, currently-shipping instance of 'each sender rolls its own HTML,' with a real rendering-risk bug attached, not just a consistency nit.

areas.non_technical_user_can: A non-technical user CAN do exactly one thing end-to-end without touching code: in crm7, go to Communications -> Templates -> New Template, type a Name, pick Email or SMS, optionally type a Subject and a Category/Description, and type a Body into a plain textarea using {{first_name}}-style placeholders (auto-detected and shown as badges) -- Save. Then in Compose Message, pick that template from a dropdown (prefills Subject/Body), edit the recipient/sender, and click Send or Save Draft. That is the full ceiling of no-code authoring in this codebase. They CANNOT apply bold, italic, links, images, buttons, or any layout to that body -- it is one plain-text field, sent verbatim as both body_html and body_text (crm7/src/lib/communications.ts:131-132), so literal markdown syntax like **bold** or a raw anchor tag would ship exactly as typed, unrendered, with no live preview of the actual rendered email. They cannot see, edit, or even know about the branded D2C shell (colors, gradient header, logo) that wraps platform sends -- that lives entirely in Deno source (business-suite-unified/supabase/functions/_shared/email-layout.ts) with zero UI. They have no access whatsoever to: the Supabase Auth system emails (password reset, invite, signup, magic link, email-change -- editable only via the external Supabase project Dashboard by someone with Supabase admin credentials), the invoice email, the charge-rate-quote-signing email, the lead-capture confirmation email, the tenant-invite email, the tester-license email, jodie's PR-notify email, or send-notification's 4 canned templates (welcome/invoice/alert/reminder) -- every one of those bodies is a hardcoded string inside a TypeScript/Deno edge-function file that requires a developer with repo write access and Supabase edge-function deploy rights to change, then a fresh deploy to take effect.
gaps: No rich-text/WYSIWYG anywhere in the whole surface -- every authoring field (communication_templates body, compose body, docs/email-templates HTML files) is either a raw plain-text textarea or hand-written HTML in source; there is no in-between and no non-technical path to a formatted email.

Two parallel, disconnected 'template' database tables (communication_templates with a working UI, email_templates with full backend CRUD but a dead-code-only UI) that were never reconciled -- email-dispatcher's server-side template lookup queries email_templates, so template_id values coming from crm7's actual compose flow (which reference communication_templates) silently fail to resolve.

The one shared branding asset (_shared/email-layout.ts renderEmail shell) is pure code with no UI, applies inconsistently (only to source:'platform' fragment sends through email-dispatcher/send-notification), and is bypassed entirely by any function that builds its own full html document -- at least two do (assign-tester-license, invoice-send-direct), and invoice-send-direct's version uses CSS/color techniques (style blocks, flexbox/grid, oklch()) the shell's own documentation says are broken in Outlook/Gmail.

what_exists.name: Merge-field/token mechanism in R80.4, braden, throughput
what_exists.path: n/a — grepped all three for \{\{[a-zA-Z_]+\}\} and %VAR% patterns in *.ts/*.tsx under src/
what_exists.detail: Zero hits in any of the three apps. No template-variable, merge-field, or placeholder-substitution mechanism of any kind exists in these three apps' source trees.

areas.non_technical_user_can: Across all six apps, there is exactly one place where a non-technical user (no markdown, no code, no knowledge of {{...}} syntax) can insert a merge field: conduit's Settings → Email Templates section, where clicking a labeled button (e.g. "Candidate Name") inserts the correct token at the cursor. For the Google Docs document-merge system (the only fully working merge pipeline, used for apprentice/host-employer PDFs), authoring happens entirely outside the app in Google Docs, and even the underlying merge_variables configuration that maps a key like host_employer.address to a real column has no in-app editor at all (the 'Register Template' button is a dead link) — a non-technical user cannot create or edit a mail-merge document template without an engineer writing SQL. Worse, in crm7's actual send flow (Compose Message) and its EmailComposeDialog whole-template picker, even a user who correctly types or pastes {{first_name}} will have that literal text delivered unresolved to the real recipient, because no caller populates the template_data the shared substitution engine needs — so the one UI hint that looks like a working merge-field feature is functionally broken end-to-end.
gaps: No unified/shared field-picker component exists — at least 4 divergent implementations across crm7 and conduit (regex-detect-after-typing in 3 places, one real click-to-insert picker in 1 place, plus the entirely separate Google-Docs-external-authoring model), none of them sharing code.

The one working click-to-insert picker (conduit EmailTemplatesSection) is hardcoded to a fixed list of 13 variable keys with no connection to any entity schema/registry, and — critically — is not reachable from the actual send flow (ComposeDialog.tsx has no template/variable support at all).

Document-template merge-variable authoring (crm7 document_templates.merge_variables) has zero UI — the 'Register Template' route is dead — so the richest field-mapping engine in the estate (composite fields: full_name, formatted address, ANZSCO, qualification_name) is entirely SQL/migration-only to configure.

Real server-side {{var}}->value substitution exists in exactly one place estate-wide (business-suite-unified's shared email-dispatcher substituteVariables()), but no caller in crm7 or conduit ever populates template_data, so the substitution never actually fires in production sends — merge tokens go out to real recipients unresolved.

crm7's Mail Merge batch feature implies bulk generate-and-send to many recipients but has no backend processor anywhere in the codebase and no recipient-selection UI — batches are created and then permanently stuck at status='pending'.

No entity-aware 'available fields for this record type' concept is surfaced anywhere in the UI — a user composing a message to an Apprentice has no way to discover which fields (first_name, employer.address, etc.) are even legal to reference.
R80.4, braden, and throughput have no merge-field capability whatsoever, so any unified authoring system would be greenfield for those three apps.
reusable_assets: conduit's insertVariable() cursor-splice pattern (EmailTemplatesSection.tsx:130-146) — a proven, accessible, non-technical-friendly button-to-textarea-cursor insertion mechanism; the right base to generalize into a shared @bsuite package component.

Three near-duplicate extractVariables()/extractTemplateVariables() pure functions (crm7 template-create.tsx, template-edit.tsx; conduit admin/templates/constants.ts) that already do literal (non-regex-per-BSuite-rules) {{...}} token scanning — trivially consolidatable into one shared, tested function.

crm7's document_templates.merge_variables schema + resolveField() composite-field resolver (generate-document/index.ts:476-560) — the most sophisticated field-mapping engine in the estate (handles nested/derived fields like formatted address and combined code+title); a real field-picker UI could be built by exposing this mapping via an RPC/API instead of leaving it edge-function-internal.

business-suite-unified's shared email_templates table (columns: variables jsonb array of {name, description}) and its working substituteVariables() engine — the substitution mechanism itself is sound; it only needs (a) an authoring UI (currently none) and (b) every caller wired to actually pass template_data.

The existing @bsuite/* npm-published shared-package pattern (page-builder, theme, nav-core, charge-calc) is architectural precedent for shipping a new @bsuite/merge-fields package so crm7 and conduit stop reinventing this independently.

what_exists.detail: Renders the AI assistant's chat replies as read-only markdown. Unrelated to document authoring — confirmed by grep, this is the only react-markdown/remark/rehype usage in the estate; there is no markdown *editor* surface anywhere.

areas.non_technical_user_can: Today a non-technical user can either (a) upload a .docx/.doc/.pdf as an opaque attachment via a metadata form (title, category, access level, storage bucket) and later download the unchanged original — no in-app preview or editing, or (b) if a developer/admin has already hand-authored a template directly in Google Docs (typing {{FIELD_NAME}} placeholders themselves) and pasted its Google Doc ID into crm7's 'Register Template' form, the user can pick that pre-built template from a dropdown and click 'Generate PDF' to merge live CRM data into it and download/sign the result. What a non-technical user CANNOT do is upload their own existing Word document and turn it into an editable, merge-field-enabled template inside BSuite — there is no in-app viewer, no in-app editor, no docx parser, and no visual merge-field inserter anywhere in the estate. The only 'editing' surface for a template is Google Docs itself (an external tool), and creating a merge field there requires manually typing raw {{...}} syntax — arguably a higher bar than the markdown the operator already rejects as too technical.
gaps: Zero docx/doc/odt/rtf parsing libraries anywhere in the 6-app estate (mammoth, docx, docxtemplater, pandoc, officegen all absent from every package.json and lockfile) — nothing can read the CONTENTS of an uploaded Word file, only store its raw bytes.
Zero WYSIWYG/rich-text editor package anywhere (no Tiptap/Slate/Lexical/Quill/CKEditor) to build an in-app document editor on top of.

No merge-field UI (field picker, autocomplete, 'insert field' button) exists anywhere; every merge-field mechanism in the estate is either hand-typed {{TOKEN}} text in an external Google Doc, or a hardcoded server-side resolver function (resolveField() in generate-document/index.ts) that only understands a fixed, developer-defined set of entity fields.

The one schema element that gestures at 'upload a docx and use it as a template' (document_templates.source='uploaded_docx', uploaded_file_path) is a dead stub with no implementing code — not a partial feature, unreachable from any UI or edge function.

Document template authoring/editing is entirely outsourced to Google Workspace (WIF-authenticated Google Docs/Drive API) — there is no BSuite-native document composition surface at all; if a tenant has no Google Docs access, template authoring is impossible.
No in-app preview exists for uploaded Office documents (no Google Docs Viewer iframe, no Office Online embed, no docx-to-HTML render) — users must download the file locally to view it.

The Collaborative Documents Monaco editor cannot import an uploaded file of any kind and produces plaintext/code/markdown source, not formatted rich text — it is not a substitute for a word-processor-style editor even though it superficially sounds like one.
reusable_assets: Supabase Storage document buckets + RLS + document_records/document_templates tables (crm7) — tenant-scoped, virus-scanned (document-virus-scan edge fn), already handle the 'store the raw file' half of any future upload-and-edit flow.
FileUploadZone component (crm7/src/components/common/FileUploadZone.tsx) — reusable, virus-scan/size-limit-aware upload widget already wired into multiple pages.

pdf-lib generation/annotation patterns (documentSigner.ts, offerDocuments.ts) — proven for the 'render final PDF' output stage of any future compose-then-export flow.

synthesis.headline: There is no document-authoring system in BSuite — there are nine half-systems, and the two that look most complete (Google Docs merge, mail merge) are provably dead in production: the deployed `generate-document` function is business-suite-unified's flat-HTML one, not crm7's Google Docs merger; the live `document_templates` table has no `google_doc_id`/`merge_variables`/`signing_config` columns at all and 0 rows; and `mail_merge_batches` does not exist as a table. The one genuinely promising foundation is newer than the audit assumed: crm7 already ships Plate.js v53 (`platejs` 53.2.4) wired to org_documents — several per-area reports grepped only for tiptap/slate/lexical/quill and wrongly concluded "no rich-text editor exists anywhere in the estate". It does exist, it is routed, and it is the right thing to build on — but today it renders with no toolbar, no list plugin, and no way to insert a heading, table or merge field by clicking, so in practice it is a bold/italic/underline-by-keyboard box.
synthesis.can_user_upload_docx_today: No — and not close. A user can upload a .docx and download the same bytes back, nothing more. Verified: zero Word-parsing libraries exist anywhere in the six-app estate (grepped every package.json for mammoth, docx, docxtemplater, pizzip, officegen, html-to-docx, turndown — zero matches), so no code in BSuite can read the CONTENTS of a Word file. There is no in-app viewer either: crm7/src/pages/documents/[id].tsx offers only a Download button. The schema does gesture at this — crm7/supabase/migrations/20260304000006_template_self_service.sql defines `document_templates.source = 'uploaded_docx'` and an `uploaded_file_path` column commented "For DOCX uploads stored in Supabase Storage before Google Docs conversion" — but grep of the entire crm7 tree (app + edge functions) returns zero references to either outside that migration file, and the live `document_templates` table does not even have those columns. It is a stub column with no implementing code. What DOES work today is opaque storage: 425 live rows in `document_metadata` (encrypted, virus-scanned, verification-workflowed compliance file uploads via DocumentHub.tsx) — that is the only part of this space with real production usage, and it is filing-cabinet capability, not authoring.
synthesis.merge_field_reality: A merge-field mechanism exists in four incompatible flavours, and a non-coder can usefully reach exactly one of them — in one app, on one screen, for one artefact type. (1) The most sophisticated engine — resolveField() in crm7/supabase/functions/generate-document/index.ts, which resolves composite fields like full_name, formatted address, ANZSCO code+title — is unreachable in production three separate ways: that source file is not the function deployed under the `generate-document` slug (business-suite-unified's is, confirmed via list_edge_functions, and it 400s on crm7's payload shape); the `document_templates` row shape it reads does not exist in the live database; and there are 0 template rows. (2) The shared server-side substituteVariables() in email-dispatcher is real and deployed, but it only fires when `template_id` resolves against `email_templates` — and crm7's compose flow passes a `communication_templates` id into that lookup, so it silently misses, and no caller in crm7 or conduit ever populates `template_data`. Net effect: a user who types {{first_name}} in crm7's Compose Message gets that literal text delivered to a real recipient, unresolved. (3) Three near-duplicate extractVariables() regex scanners (crm7 template-create, template-edit, conduit admin/templates) detect tokens AFTER you type them and show read-only badges — they help you check your typing, they do not help you author. (4) The only true non-technical merge-field UI in the estate is conduit/src/components/settings/EmailTemplatesSection.tsx: 13 human-labelled buttons that splice {{key}} in at the cursor. It is the right pattern and the wrong everything else — the list is hardcoded with no connection to any schema, it is not reachable from conduit's actual send dialog (ComposeDialog.tsx has no template support at all), and the store behind it writes to a `body` column that does not exist on the live `email_templates` table (verified: the real columns are body_html/body_text), so the first time a user clicks Save it fails at PostgREST. Everywhere else, "insert a merge field" means hand-typing a case-sensitive {{TOKEN}} into a Google Doc or a plain textarea, having somehow already learned the exact key — a strictly higher bar than the markdown the operator has already ruled out.

synthesis.recommended_shape: Build ONE authoring surface, shipped as a shared package, where the non-technical user never sees syntax of any kind — no markdown, no HTML, no {{ }}. Concretely: a Plate.js editor with a visible toolbar (bold, italic, heading, bullet/numbered list, table, link, image) and an "Insert field" button beside it. Clicking Insert field opens a searchable list of plain-English labels scoped to what the document is about — "Apprentice's first name", "Host employer trading name", "Weekly charge rate", "Today's date" — and drops a coloured pill into the text. The pill is a Plate mention node (@platejs/mention is already installed), so the user sees "Apprentice's first name", never a token; a Preview toggle swaps every pill for real data from a chosen record. That one interaction is the whole answer to "even markdown is too much", and it is also the answer to "insert a merge field". Store every authored body as Plate jsonb in ONE table — extend org_documents (already Plate-shaped, correctly RLS'd, 0 rows so it is free to reshape) rather than adding a fourth document table; give it a kind discriminator covering policy, handbook, contract, letter, email. Render that one content model three ways: to HTML through the existing _shared/email-layout.ts shell for email, to PDF through @react-pdf/renderer (already proven by ChargeRatePdfDocument), and to screen through the existing portal viewer. Feed the field picker and the renderer from ONE field catalogue — lift resolveField()'s composite logic out of the undeployed edge function into a shared resolver plus an RPC that enumerates available fields per entity type. Then route every existing send/generate path through it: crm7 Compose, conduit /admin/templates, conduit's offer letter and training contract (whose wording is currently TypeScript string literals — the highest-value single win in the estate), the invoice email, the quote email. On Word: be honest with him. Do NOT promise round-trip .docx editing — that is a genuinely hard problem (headers/footers, numbered clause schemes, nested tables, tracked changes) and nothing in the estate does it. Offer one-way IMPORT: upload a .docx, we convert it once into an editable BSuite document, and from then on BSuite is the source of truth. Two viable routes, both cheap: Google Drive's files.create with convert=true using the WIF auth crm7 already has working, or add mammoth (docx to HTML) and map HTML to Plate blocks. Formatting fidelity will be imperfect on complex legal documents and he should hear that before it surprises him. On size: this is not a week. Phase 1 (toolbar + field picker + one content model + email and PDF render, crm7 only) is a solid multi-week build. Phase 2 (conduit adopts it; offer letter and training contract become editable templates; DOCX import) is comparable again. Phase 3 (versioning with re-acknowledgement on edit, approval workflow, bulk merge send, live co-authoring via the existing YJS transport) is more. Crucially, roughly half the perceived work is deletion, not construction — mail_merge_batches (table does not exist), the crm7 Google-Docs generate-document path (not deployed, schema missing, 0 rows), email_templates-vs-communication_templates (pick communication_templates, migrate the other), cms_documents and cms_posts (zero code references), braden's two dead editors, and the /documents/hub versus DocumentHub.tsx naming collision should all go before anything new is built on top of them.
open_questions_for_operator: Google Workspace — in or out? The WIF keyless auth is genuinely built and working, but keeping Google Docs means document authoring lives outside BSuite permanently and every tenant needs Workspace access. My recommendation is to cut it and author natively in Plate, but that is your call because it also decides whether we fix or delete crm7's generate-document.

DOCX import fidelity — what loss is acceptable? A one-way import will approximate complex Word layout (headers/footers, auto-numbered clause schemes, nested tables). For a marketing letter that is fine; for a training contract or a host services agreement you may need the original preserved byte-exact as the legal artefact with BSuite holding only an editable derivative. Which documents must stay pixel-faithful?

Who owns the legal wording? crm7 has a DeployScopeSelector pattern for platform-versus-tenant templates with locking. Should a GTO tenant be free to edit a training contract or offer letter template, or should those be platform-locked and only overridable with compliance sign-off? This shapes the schema, not just the UI.

Handbook re-acknowledgement — today updateOrgDocument() patches content in place and nothing invalidates prior acknowledgements, so an apprentice's 'read' stays true against wording they never saw. Should any edit to a published, acknowledged document force re-acknowledgement, or only edits you explicitly mark material? This is a compliance judgement, not a technical one.

Signing — consolidate onto one system or keep several? There are four (charge-rate token links with 5 live rows, conduit's r7 e-sign substrate, crm7's orphaned pdf-lib signer with the AU ETA 1999 audit page, and training-plan TripleSignOff). The orphaned crm7 signer has the strongest legal reasoning but zero usage. Is a single 'send any document to any external party for signature' capability worth building, or is charge-rate quotes genuinely the only external-signature case?

Email brand shell — mandatory for everything? The D2C shell currently applies only to platform-source fragment sends and is bypassed by any function shipping full HTML. Should it become non-bypassable including for sends from a person's own connected mailbox, or do user-mailbox sends stay unbranded plain text by design?

Supabase Auth system emails (password reset, invite, magic link) live only in the external Supabase dashboard, and that drift already caused a real account-lockout (fixed in git today as 6df70da2, dashboard paste still outstanding). Do you want these brought into the product as first-class editable templates, or is a CI check that diffs the live dashboard config against the repo copy sufficient?

Which apps actually need to AUTHOR versus only RENDER? braden, throughput and R80.4 have zero capability today. Adding read-only rendering is cheap; adding authoring to each is not. Is 'crm7 and conduit author, everyone else renders' the right boundary?
